title: Outline stitch
subtitle: A fine, twisted line stitch worked with the thread kept below the needle
excerpt: Outline stitch produces a smooth, tightly twisted line along any curved or straight path. It is worked like stem stitch but with the thread held below the needle rather than above it, which reverses the twist. The stitch is a staple for outlining motifs, lettering and fine detail work.
sourceNotes: Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), outline stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882). Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870).

glossaryTerms.definition: The drawn or traced line on the fabric that guides where the stitches go.

content.text: Outline stitch is a line stitch from the stem stitch family, used wherever a fine, firm outline is needed. It is worked along a

by taking small overlapping stitches forward while keeping the thread below the needle. This produces a twist that lies on the opposite side from stem stitch. On a straight line the two stitches are almost identical in appearance; on a curve, outline stitch naturally follows the inner edge of the curve. It is used for lettering, floral outlines and any motif edge where a thin, clean line is needed.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 1 or 2 strands for a fine outline

content.text: Secure the thread on the back and bring the needle up at point A, at the left end of the line.

Hold the thread below the line of work (away from you if the line runs left to right). Insert the needle down at point B, roughly 4 mm ahead along the line, and bring it back up at point C, halfway between A and B (about 2 mm back from B). The needle exits the fabric midway along the previous stitch.
Pull the thread through. Keep it below the needle as you draw it to the right. You will see a twisted cord beginning to form along the line.
Repeat: insert at a new point D, roughly 4 mm ahead, and come back up at point B (the previous entry point). Always bring the needle up at the hole made by the last down-stitch of the previous step.
Continue along the line. Keep the thread below the needle on every stitch; switching to above the needle changes the stitch to stem stitch and reverses the twist. At the end, fasten off on the back.

items.symptom: The line looks scraggly with no consistent twist
items.cause: The thread position keeps switching between above and below the needle
items.fix: Before each stitch, check that the thread is below the needle. Consistency on every single stitch is what builds the twist.

items.symptom: The line wanders off the drawn outline
items.cause: The needle is coming up in a new hole rather than back into the previous stitch's entry point
items.fix: The needle must re-enter the exact hole made by the last down-stitch. Use that hole as a guide and angle the needle to emerge there.
